chunks: And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad [Abdullah ibn Sinan], from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Nasibi (one who is hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt) is not merely one who has enmity towards us, the People of the House, because you will not find a man who says, 'I am the Nasibi [I hate] Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.' Rather, the Nasibi is one who has enmity towards you, and he knows that you love us and that you are from our Shias.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: Ahl al-Bayt; the People of the House (Prophet's family)
key_terms.النَّاصِبُ: Nasibi; one who is hostile or inimical, specifically to the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What is the true definition of a Nasibi according to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) refines the concept of *Nasibi* by shifting the focus from general hostility to specific, conscious enmity directed at the Shia for their allegiance to the Ahl al-Bayt. This distinction highlights that true enmity is defined by the awareness of one's opposition to the Prophet's family and the deliberate rejection of their *Wilayah*, a key criterion in Shia jurisprudence for identifying distinct opponents. The hadith underscores that mere ignorance or general dislike does not constitute the status of *Nasibi*, but rather a targeted animosity rooted in the denial of their spiritual authority.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 4. And from the previous chain from Muhammad b. Ahmad from Ibrahim b. Ishaq from Abdillah b. Hamad [Abdillah b. Sinan] from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “

One who is inimical of we. Ahle Bayt (a.s.) is not a Nasibi because there is no such unfortunate person in this world who says that he is inimical and hateful to Muhammad and his progeny. Rather, Nasibi is one who has enmity with you because he knows that you love us and are our Shias.”
